name: Dennis Hopper

notes.name: Wikipedia · Dennis Hopper
notes.q: He was involved in L.A.'s Ferus and Virginia Dwan galleries in the 1960s, and he was a longtime friend and supporter to New York dealer Tony Shafrazi.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Dennis Hopper
notes.q: The title of the exhibition, Double Standard, was taken from Hopper's iconic 1961 photograph of the two Standard Oil signs seen through an automobile windshield at the intersection of Santa Monica Boulevard, Melrose Avenue, and North Doheny Drive on historic Route 66 in Los Angeles.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Dennis Hopper
notes.q: Journalist Ann Hornaday wrote: "With its portrait of counterculture heroes raising their middle fingers to the uptight middle-class hypocrisies, Easy Rider became the cinematic symbol of the 1960s, a celluloid anthem to freedom, macho bravado and anti-establishment rebellion".

src.name: Wikipedia · Dennis Hopper
src.q: In 1959, Hopper moved to New York to study Method acting under Lee Strasberg at the Actors Studio.

src.name: Wikipedia · Dennis Hopper
src.q: He spent much of the 1970s and early 1980s living as an "outcast" in Taos, New Mexico, after the success of Easy Rider.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Dennis Hopper
notes.q: In March 2010, it was announced that Hopper was on the "short list" for Jeffrey Deitch's inaugural show at the Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles (MOCA).
